checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Final video stays 7 s with original cockpit footage at original speed and framing
must.why: Output is 7 s and the cockpit shots look unchanged in framing and pacing.

must.item: Narrator speaks the exact supplied script, no omissions or additions
Speech starts within 0.5 s and 'home' finishes in the last half-second uncut
must.why: Timing cannot be heard. The script is long for 7 s at 0.95x speed, so a cutoff is a risk.

must.item: Delivery calm and intelligible, no rushed speech or stretching artifacts
must.why: Audio cannot be judged. Fitting the script into 7 s may force fast delivery.

must.item: Original radio calls and other sounds absent; no added music or on-screen text
must.why: Burned-in captions 'Rook, you with me?' and 'Right here, Vega.' appear in the frames at 2.8 s and 4.9 s. The user asked for no captions.

exact_text.text: Above the clouds, every second counts. Stay focused, trust your training, and bring everyone safely home.
exact_text.read_as: No script text is on screen. The only on-screen text is 'Rook, you with me?' and 'Right here, Vega.'

faults.what: Burned-in subtitles from the old radio calls ('Rook, you with me?', 'Right here, Vega.') remain. The user explicitly said no captions, and they no longer match the new voiceover.
The agent used the lip-sync tool and a 60 s end time, which cost 1,800 credits. The mouth is hidden behind a mask, so lip-sync gave no benefit.

summary: The 7 s cockpit clip kept its length and framing, but it still has burned-in captions from the old dialogue, which the user explicitly ruled out, so it needs a redo; the voiceover itself could not be checked.
